conventions.convention: The geometry is an actual product metric dx₁² ⊕ g₀ on a compact smooth domain contained in ℝ × M₀ interior, in dimension at least three. A conformal factor is excluded. Orientability is not assumed. The Laplacian is Δg = divg ∇g.

Sobolev norms use a fixed finite atlas and partition; H₀¹ is the closure of compactly supported interior smooth functions. The complex H⁻¹/² space is the conjugate-linear dual, with pairing linear in the dual element and conjugate-linear in the boundary test. Empty boundaries and dimensions zero and one have explicit separate conventions.

Conductivity DN data are the full physical outward flux γ∂νu; Schrödinger DN data are ∂νu. Schrödinger potentials are real, smooth, and have trivial zero-Dirichlet kernel. Equality means equality on every H¹/² boundary input.

Ray injectivity concerns compactly supported smooth scalar functions and all unit-speed boundary-to-boundary segments with strictly inward initial velocity, strictly outward terminal velocity, and interior intermediate points. Complex injectivity is interpreted separately on real and imaginary parts.
Euclidean CGO solutions use exp(iζ·x), with a complex-bilinear null condition ζ·ζ = 0 and the Hermitian length |ζ|. Their correction has O(|ζ|⁻¹) L² norm and bounded L² gradient.
Boundary jets use inward distance xₙ, whereas DN derivatives use the outward normal. The weighted boundary concentration constant is cₖ = k!/2ᵏ.
The cubic small-data maps use real finite-dimensional parameters, allow complex smooth boundary directions, and select the unique solution in a fixed small Hˢ ball, with integer s > n/2 + 2.

The four-factor witnesses may depend on Q and may be constant in τ; no uniform concentration family, nonzero-witness condition, or quantitative remainder is asserted. The proof imports harmonic-product density, checked against [LLLS Proposition 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.12562).

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. On a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, a real smooth q with trivial weak H₀¹ Dirichlet kernel gives a unique H¹ solution of (−Δg + q)u = F with prescribed H¹/² trace for every F ∈ L². For zero trace and F ∈ Hᵐ, u ∈ Hᵐ⁺² with norm bounded by Cₘ‖F‖Hᵐ. Smooth forcing and boundary data give membership in every integer Sobolev space.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. On a compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary and smooth positive γ, the zero-boundary Poincaré inequality holds. For every h ∈ L² and f ∈ H¹/² there is a unique H¹ function with trace f satisfying ∫γg(∇v,∇conj(z)) = −∫h conj(z) for every z ∈ H₀¹. Smooth data give a solution smooth up to the boundary.

Under AC and Countable Choice, positive smooth scalar conductivities and real smooth nonresonant Schrödinger potentials define full weak DN maps H¹/²(∂M) → H⁻¹/²(∂M) by their boundary energy forms. For smooth data these are γ∂νout v and ∂νout u, respectively.

For smooth boundary data on the stated compact connected domain, the difference of physical conductivity DN pairings is ∫(γ₁−γ₂)g(∇u₁,∇conj(u₂)); for real smooth nonresonant Schrödinger potentials it is ∫(q₁−q₂)u₁conj(u₂). AC and Countable Choice are assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. For n ≥ 3, bounded smooth Ω contained in B(0,R), bounded complex q, and every sufficiently large null ζ, there is rζ ∈ H¹ such that exp(iζ·x)(1+rζ) solves (−Δ+q)u = 0, with ‖rζ‖₂ ≤ C|ζ|⁻¹‖q‖₂ and ‖∇rζ‖₂ ≤ C‖q‖₂; constants depend only on n, R, and ‖q‖∞.

Under AC and Countable Choice, on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain of dimension at least two, the stated common-phase boundary quasimodes for two positive smooth conductivities have arbitrary polynomial residual decay, uniformly bounded nonvanishing H¹ norms, exact H¹ corrections of the same decay order, and the weighted gradient-product limit cₖ∫∂ΩF|χ|² with cₖ = k!/2ᵏ.

For any unit-speed nontangential segment on a compact smooth Riemannian transversal, every real λ and K > 0 admit smooth vτ+iλ with residual O(τ⁻ᴷ), bounded L² norm, and |vτ+iλ|² converging against continuous tests to the ray measure weighted by exp(−2λt). No orientation or boundary condition is required.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. On the stated three-dimensional product domain with simple surface transversal, for every p, transverse geodesic pair meeting only at p, real ξ, and smooth Q, four exact harmonic H¹ witnesses give the longitudinal Fourier integral over Iₚ as their product-integral limit, multiplied by |sin(angle)|⁻¹.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. For positive smooth γ, ρ = √γ and q = Δgρ/ρ, multiplication by ρ transforms conductivity solutions to Schrödinger solutions, q has trivial Dirichlet kernel, and Λγf = ρbΛq(ρbf) − ρb(∂νoutρ)f.

concerns.concern: Proof 5.2 displays a uniform expansion on 0 ≤ xₙ ≤ λ⁻¹/² with remainder exp(−2λxₙ)[O(1)+O(λxₙ)]. From Im Φ = xₙ + O(xₙ²), the leading gradient product also has a phase-error contribution exp(−2λxₙ)O(λ²xₙ²), which is not covered by that displayed remainder throughout the asserted interval. At xₙ = λ⁻¹/², a nonzero quadratic imaginary-phase coefficient changes the leading term by order λ relative to exp(−2λxₙ), whereas the displayed remainder is only O(√λ). The subsequent rescaling argument explicitly includes the missing t²/λ phase error and closes the limit; the displayed expansion needs to agree with that argument.
